summary: Bumping consumer-verify-tuple contract v1->v2 across producer (evidence.mjs CONTRACT), consumer (decide.mjs default tupleContract), both workflows, contract tests, and docs keeps the daily tuple recovery working, and a hard-cutover policy (v1 artifacts -> non-target) is sufficient without a dual-accept window

Inventory on main 7124f0b2 found 14 v1 pin sites: evidence.mjs:63, decide.mjs:40/59/1424, daily-ci.yml:24/110/148, consumer-verify.yml:12/709/1250/1287, 4 test files, development-environment.md:100/134/135. schemaVersion 2 and Case schema v2 lane vocabulary were already fixed by rf294 — only the contract string moves

Design point (a): hard cutover. classifyRunEvidence already classifies contract mismatch as non-target (proven different tuple); a dual-accept set would only matter for a days-wide window since tuple SHAs move daily, and would let v1 evidence cover a v2 candidate — contrary to the bump's purpose. --tuple-contract/DAILY_TUPLE_CONTRACT remain the override escape hatch

Design point (b): keep schemaVersion/lanes unchecked in decide.mjs. The consumer needs tuple identity + consumer status only; evidence-internal vocabulary is validated producer-side by assertLaneRecord at finalize. The contract string is the negotiated version axis — recorded in decide.mjs header comment and development-environment.md

Repaired the stale regex to #[0-9]+ — the contract under test is 'a not_run row carrying owner attribution', not specific issue numbers which churn with #629-#631 real-run updates. Workflow lane rows and owner notes untouched
